messages:
alex: Heads-up — after landing kernel-selector v2.3 yesterday we started seeing a p99 jump in prod on the inference GPU pool. p50 unchanged, p95 +6ms, p99 +110ms. Not subtle.

jamie: thanks alex. any cluster/region specific?

alex: seen in us-west-2 and eu-central. Correlates with increase in long-context requests (>=8k tokens) + large microbatches.

nina: is this the change that switched to the new kernel path for mixed quantized ops?

alex: yes. selector now prefers fused-kernel when batch_size>1 and seq_len>1024. It seems great generally but a few traces show kernel compile/patch path triggering and stalling other microbatches.

sam: perf-bot posted a flamegraph earlier: https://perf.redwood/example/175888 - shows long GPU stall at kernel-init.

perf-bot: Auto-profile attached: peak GPU occupancy drops during kernel-init, NVTX events cluster at kernel-selection.

ryan: my hunch: some requests with very long context cause heavy KV cache misses and force a fallback to the less-optimized attention kernel which has much higher latency for long sequences. That plus microbatch aggregation is making the tail much worse.

jamie: can you paste the trace snippet?

alex: sure: ```
[GPU] 0.000s - enqueue batch
[GPU] 0.003s - kernel-select start
[GPU] 0.085s - compile/fallback path
[GPU] 0.200s - kernel exec
[GPU] 0.280s - complete
```

nina: wow compile/fallback path is huge there. We thought selector was warm at runtime. Might be interaction with new microbatch flush policy.

sam: right now scheduler waits up to `--microbatch-age-ms=25` to fill batch. For low qps, that increases head-of-line for long requests that trigger heavy kernels.

ryan: proposal: add two immediate mitigations: 1) short-lived microbatch age for requests with seq_len>2048 (`--microbatch-age-ms=5`), 2) apply soft `max_tokens` cap for public pool to reject/route very long contexts to dedicated capacity.

alex: +1. Also add a temporary kernel fallback rule: prefer older stable kernel for requests where seq_len>4096 until we fix the compile stall. config flag `kernel_preference: legacy_for_long_seq`.

jamie: operationally: can we implement as a routing policy so we don't touch SDK? e.g., traveler: if seq_len>4096 -> route to legacy kernel nodes.

nina: on KV cache: I saw eviction pressure spikes. Long contexts blow KV working set and cause repeated cache misses which increases end-to-end time. We should consider aggressive prefix pruning for very long prompts (truncate to last 2048 tokens for cached paths).

sam: actionable checklist:
- alex: temp route rule to legacy kernel for seq_len>4096 (canary to 10% traffic)
- ryan: microbatch-age override for long-ctx requests + add dynamic batch size cap (max_batch_size=16 for sequences>1024)
- nina: implement prefix-prune policy that limits cached KV to last 2048 tokens when context >4096
- jamie: push temporary `max_tokens` soft cap of 4096 with 429 fallback to hosted customers and docs note

alex: I'll open the canary patch now. jamie, set the alerting on p99 delta >50ms and on kernel-init spikes.

jamie: doing it. setting alert: runtime.kernel_init_duration.p99 > 80ms for 5m -> paged.

ryan: one more suggestion: add an age-based microbatch flush (evict oldest if any request waiting >X ms) instead of pure size threshold. reduces H-O-L when mixed latency profiles co-exist.

nina: agree. Implementing age-based plus per-request severity flag (`latency_sensitive`) so clients can opt-in/route later. For now we can auto-flag requests with short prompts as low-cost and long ones as high-cost.

sam: any objection to lowering `--microbatch-age-ms` default to 10ms for hosted pool until we validate?

alex: no objection. Do that as a temporary knob and rollback option.

jamie: summary of short-term mitigation plan posted in infra runbook under 'microbatch-degradation-playbook'. Will update with timelines. :spiral_calendar: 

alex: thanks team. if we don't see improvement after canary, we'll revert kernel-selector change and deep-dive on kernel compile caching.

nina: note for later: we should improve profiler to attribute p99 regressions to (a) kernel-init vs (b) kernel-exec vs (c) kvcache-eviction. Current metrics lump them together which hides the true root cause.

ryan: I'll add those finer-grained NVTX markers in next profiler build.

jamie: closing loop: owners assigned. I'll post a follow-up thread with canary link and quick rollback steps once alex's PR is live. :thumbsup:
